messages:
julia: Anyone else hitting streaming hang on Node edge (Vercel) where the ReadableStream never closes? Customer flow returns chunks for ~2s then nothing; client waits forever.

kevin: which SDK + runtime? any request ids?

julia: Using @redwood/sdk v0.10.0 in an edge function (Node 18 runtime / Vercel Edge). Minimal code:```ts
const res = await client.responses.stream({ input: prompt });
for await (const chunk of res) { /* push to SSE */ }
```
It streams a few tokens, then upstream stops sending the terminal event. No 5xx in logs.

support: can you paste the request-id / trace-id from the API response headers if available? also any client-side console errors?

julia: Request header trace: x-rd-request: rd-7abc1234. Client side shows no error; fetch just stalls. Server logs show a retry: 
```
2026-11-02T17:02:11Z INFO request rd-7abc1234 started
2026-11-02T17:02:12Z WARN auth failed token-refresh 401
2026-11-02T17:02:12Z INFO retry attempt 1
2026-11-02T17:02:12Z INFO request rd-7abc1234 finished (partial)
```
Looks like auth rotated mid-stream and SDK retried.

alex: this rings a bell. v0.10 had a bug where the retry logic re-used a Response.body/readable stream or called fetch.clone() incorrectly in edge contexts, which can leave the original ReadableStream locked in a 'readable' state and never closed on the client.

helen: is this reproducible locally with a simple edge-like harness? Vercel edge has different stream semantics than node server.

julia: I made a tiny repro using the edge-runtime polyfill and a fake token rotator. Steps: 1) call responses.stream 2) simulate 401 from auth provider mid-request 3) SDK issues retry -> hang. Repo link: https://git.example/repro/edge-stream-leak (private)

kevin: thanks, can you include minimal logs showing headers for the retry attempt? specifically: Authorization header, x-rd-retry, x-rd-request.

julia: pasted excerpt above. Also noticed the customer is on our dedicated infra; SLA hit (high latency) so flagged by support.

alex: short-term workaround: pin SDK to v0.11.2 which fixes retry handling for edge and avoids reusing body streams. If upgrading is not possible, workaround is to disable automatic retries for streaming calls and implement an idempotent resume token or re-fetch chunks from server side. Example patch:```ts
// disable built-in streaming retry
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey, retry: { retries: 0 } });
const res = await client.responses.stream({ input: prompt });
// manual retry: request a fresh session on 401 and restart streaming from client state
```

support: noted. I've opened a ticket RD-7893 and bumped priority to P1 for customer SLA. support-bot: link to ticket RD-7893.

support-bot: <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RD-7893|RD-7893> created and assigned to eng-runtime.

alex: I'll take the bug. Probable root cause: fetch.clone semantics on edge runtimes + our attempt to re-stream a consumed body. Fix path: ensure retry wraps a fresh ReadableStream built from buffered chunks or avoid retrying streaming requests entirely in edge runtime.

helen: can you provide a short repro branch and the exact SDK bundle hash so we can patch and backfill a hotfix?

julia: branch pushed, contains small ts fixture and Vercel config. SDK bundle: @redwood/sdk@0.10.0+sha256:abcd1234ef.

kevin: added customer notes to RD-7893, asked them to try the v0.11.2 upgrade. Customer will try later today.

julia: thanks. will update ticket after customer test. :thumbsup:

alex: follow-up: I'll add a runtime guard so streaming endpoints explicitly return a non-retriable signal when running in edge contexts. That should avoid future silent leaks. :eyes:
